technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Data Kafka to implement the Kafka-backed changelog repository for local data affinity.
Implement intelligent offset flushing using Kafka's commitSync and acknowledge mechanisms.
Implement intelligent state flushing with checkpointing and acknowledgment tracking.
Integrate Californium (Cf) library for CoAP protocol support in the source module.
Use Spring Boot configuration properties for documentation and deployment manifest representation.
Leverage Hadoop security libraries (Kerberos) for secured HDFS cluster access in Sqoop jobs.
Use Spring's RestTemplate or WebClient for Java receptor client integration with Diego runtime.
Complete deployment properties handling for Boot-based ModuleRunner in container-managed environments.
assumptions: Developers are already familiar with Spring Framework and related technologies.
Existing project structure and build tools (Maven/Gradle) are in place.
Unit and integration testing frameworks are available and configured.
Documentation templates and style guides already exist.
Security configurations for HDFS and Kerberos are pre-defined.
Diego runtime APIs and endpoints are accessible and documented.
CoAP and Kafka dependencies are compatible with Java 17+.
ModuleRunner refactoring will not require major architectural changes.

activities.activity_name: Design and implement Kafka changelog repository
activities.activity_description: Create a Spring Data repository backed by Kafka changelog to support local data affinity and off-heap stateful stream processing.
Add logic to flush Kafka offsets based on successful message acknowledgments from the module-producer.
Add logic to flush stream processing state based on successful message acknowledgments from the module-producer.
Create a CoAP source module using a lightweight protocol library to support constrained embedded environments.
Write documentation for configuring properties files to represent the deployment manifest as recommended.

activities.activity_name: Enable secured HDFS access for Sqoop jobs
activities.activity_description: Add support for running Sqoop jobs against secured HDFS clusters with proper authentication and authorization.
Develop a Java client to interact with Diego runtime using receptor REST APIs.
Finish remaining deployment properties work for Boot-based ModuleRunner to run XD in container-managed environments without xd-containers.
Perform unit, integration, and system testing across all implemented features.
